definition: Literal meaning 'Friend of the Court'. A person or organization who is not a party to the litigation but is invited by the court to advise on legal matters.
Action taken by a court on its own motion, without a formal complaint or petition from any party.
A writ (court order) requiring a person under arrest to be brought before a judge or into court, especially to secure the person's release unless lawful grounds are shown for their detention.
A matter that has been adjudicated by a competent court and therefore may not be pursued further by the same parties.
A judge's expression of opinion uttered in court or in a written judgment, but not essential to the decision and therefore not legally binding as a precedent.
The legal principle or rationale on which a judicial decision is based. This is the binding part of the judgment.
A document by which a client authorizes an advocate to represent them in a court case.
A notice filed in court by a party preventing the court from issuing an order or judgment against them without giving them a hearing.
A written document prepared by police when they receive information about the commission of a cognizable offence.
An offence for which police can arrest without a warrant and start investigation without court permission (e.g., murder, rape).
An offence for which police have no authority to arrest without a warrant and cannot investigate without a Magistrate's permission (e.g., simple hurt, defamation).
An offence where bail is a matter of right. The police officer or court must grant bail if the accused is prepared to give bail.
An offence where bail is not a right but a discretion of the court. The accused can be released on bail only by the court's order.
Bail granted by a Sessions Court or High Court to a person apprehending arrest. It becomes effective at the moment of arrest.
Right to bail that accrues to an accused if the investigation agency fails to file the charge sheet within the prescribed period (60 or 90 days).
Temporary bail granted for a short period until the final disposal of the bail application.
Bail granted to enable an accused to travel to a different jurisdiction to seek regular bail.
Temporary release of a prisoner who agrees to certain conditions before the completion of the maximum sentence period.
Leave granted to a prisoner from jail for a specified period, typically as a reward for good conduct, without any specific reason required.
Final report prepared by the police under Section 173 CrPC proving the accusation against the accused.
A judgment that a person is not guilty of the crime with which they have been charged.
A formal declaration that someone is guilty of a criminal offence, made by the verdict of a jury or the decision of a judge in a court of law.
A person who takes responsibility for another's performance of an undertaking, for example their appearing in court or paying a debt.
An accomplice who turns witness against the other accused in return for a pardon.
A witness who testifies against the party who called them to testify.
Alternative dispute resolution mechanism in India where disputes pending in courts or at pre-litigation stage are settled amicably.
Litigation introduced in a court of law not by the aggrieved party but by the court itself or by any other private party in the interest of the public.
